title: Authentication Bypass - Unauthenticated Access to getPrescriptions GraphQL Query
description: The GraphQL API endpoint at /graphql allows completely unauthenticated access to the getPrescriptions query. The resolver does not validate authentication credentials before returning prescription data. No authentication headers, tokens, or session validation is required to query sensitive prescription information. An attacker can manipulate the userId parameter to retrieve prescriptions for any user in the system without any access control checks.
impact:
Complete authentication bypass enabling:
- Unauthorized access to all prescription data in the system
- Exposure of sensitive medical information and patient data
- Information disclosure via sensitive flag fields embedded in prescription records
- User enumeration by attempting different userId values
- Potential to modify or delete prescriptions if write operations are also unprotected
- Compliance violations (HIPAA, GDPR) due to unauthorized access to PHI/PII
- Reputational damage from large-scale medical data breach
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability:
- Successfully executed unauthenticated GraphQL query: { getPrescriptions(userId: 1) { id userId prescriptionDetails flag } }
- HTTP 200 response returned without any authentication errors
- Retrieved 89 prescriptions for userId=1 containing sensitive medical information
- Prescription ID 43 included exposed flag field: flag{this_is_a_fake_flag}
- No authentication middleware validation detected
- No 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden responses encountered
- Full prescription details including descriptions and internal flags returned without credentials
remediation:
1. Implement authentication middleware at the GraphQL endpoint level that validates JWT tokens or secure session cookies for ALL incoming requests before resolver execution
2. Add authentication checks directly in the getPrescriptions query resolver to verify user identity
3. Implement object-level authorization (OBIA) to ensure users can only access their own prescription data (userId matches authenticated user)
4. Apply @auth directive on sensitive GraphQL schema definitions to enforce authentication requirements
5. Add role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict sensitive queries based on user permissions
6. Implement query-level authentication middleware using frameworks like graphql-middleware or Apollo Server plugins
7. Remove sensitive internal fields (like flag) from production GraphQL schema or restrict via authorization
8. Add logging and monitoring for unauthenticated query attempts
9. Implement rate limiting on GraphQL endpoint to prevent enumeration attacks
10. Conduct security audit of all GraphQL resolvers to identify similar authentication gaps
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, OWASP A07:2021 - Authentication Bypass, OWASP API1:2019 - Broken Object Level Authorization, CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function, CWE-862: Missing Authorization, GraphQL Security Best Practices: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/GraphQL_Cheat_Sheet.html
toolCallDescription: Document the confirmed GraphQL authentication bypass vulnerability with POC evidence
